page.layout: One printed page, cut off on this scan. The page number 278 stands at the top left. The main text block is not visible in this part. Below the page number, in a narrow column, are four marginal notes, each beginning with a reference mark (*, †, *).; One block: a heading at the top, then a ruled table in one column. Its lower rows carry names, cut off at the right edge. No margin notes, no running head, no page number.; One table, one column: left cells hold the names of the consuls ("Iidem sex." for the years 1376 to 1383, and a list of names for 1384), right cells hold the years with their reference marks. Below the table, at the lower right, the word "Herman". Running head at the top.
page.notes: The main text block is not in this part, so the marginal notes stand alone here. The marks at the start of the notes (*, †) are printed without matching marks in the visible text. Doubtful readings: "Fœdus" (first letter may be F), "Eidē" (the tilde is uncertain). The heading is cut off at the right: only "Ea/" is visible, so the "/" may be a letter or a stain. The names are cut at the right edge and are copied as far as they show. Rules without text are not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "fidem" or "Iidem" in the row for 1379; "Iidew" in the row for 1380. The marks above 1380 and 1382 are asterisks (*), the mark above 1381 is a dagger (†). The names of 1384 are fragments of lines whose first letters are not visible; they are copied as they stand. The year 1384 spans the name block and is placed beside its last lines.
